cmc_HT-101_3.2.P.pdf.grade_justification: Avicel PH-102 was selected over PH-101 because its larger median particle size (approximately 100 um) provides superior powder flow for direct compression at commercial press speeds; three engineering batches showed weight variation below 1.5% RSD.

cmc_HT-204_3.2.P.pdf.grade_justification: Avicel PH-101 was chosen for its finer particle size, which improves content uniformity of the low-dose active in the wet granulation process. Blend uniformity across development batches met the acceptance criterion of 90.0-110.0%.
guidance_cited: FDA Guidance for Industry: Nonclinical Studies for the Safety Evaluation of Pharmaceutical Excipients
cmc_HT-204_3.2.P.pdf.contradiction_detail: Submission uses Avicel PH-101; current spec requires Avicel PH-102.

cmc_HT-317_3.2.P.pdf.grade_justification: Starch 1500 was selected because its partial pregelatinization provides both filling and disintegration function in a single excipient, minimizing the number of components in the capsule fill. Dissolution exceeded 85% in 30 minutes for all registration batches.

excipient_grades: Lactose monohydrate: Ph. Eur., milled grade 200 mesh
cmc_HT-422_3.2.P.pdf.grade_justification: Milled lactose monohydrate (200 mesh) was used because it is the grade qualified at the European contract manufacturer and is compatible with the aqueous granulation process. Compatibility studies at 40C/75% RH for 3 months showed no increase in degradants.
guidance_cited: EMA Guideline on Excipients in the Dossier for Application for Marketing Authorisation of a Medicinal Product
cmc_HT-422_3.2.P.pdf.contradiction_detail: Submission uses milled lactose monohydrate (Ph. Eur.); current spec requires anhydrous lactose NF.

excipient_grades: Polysorbate 80: Super Refined, low peroxide, NF
cmc_HT-509_3.2.P.pdf.grade_justification: A low-peroxide grade of polysorbate 80 was required because dunaxitib is susceptible to oxidative degradation; standard grade lots produced oxidative degradant D-3 above the 0.2% identification threshold at 6 months accelerated.
guidance_cited: ICH Q3B(R2) Impurities in New Drug Products

cmc_HT-611_3.2.P.pdf.grade_justification: Spray-dried mannitol (Pearlitol 200 SD) was selected for its pleasant mouthfeel and compressibility, enabling disintegration in under 30 seconds per USP <701>.
guidance_cited: FDA Guidance for Industry: Orally Disintegrating Tablets

ha_letter_PMDA-2026-0115.pdf.commitment: submit dissolution profile comparison data (f2) between the registration and the proposed commercial capsule shell supplier

ha_letter_FDA-2026-0302.pdf.owner: Dr. Priya Raman, CMC Regulatory Lead

stability_protocol_SP-101-02.pdf.acceptance_criteria: Assay 95.0-105.0%; any unspecified degradant NMT 0.2%; total degradants NMT 1.0%; dissolution Q=80% at 30 minutes
stability_protocol_SP-101-02.pdf.deviations: Deviation DEV-2025-118: the 9-month long-term pull was performed 6 days late due to chamber maintenance; impact assessed as none.
stability_protocol_SP-101-02.pdf.bracketing_justification: Bracketing is applied to the 30-count and 500-count HDPE bottle presentations; the 90-count presentation is not tested because container closure and fill ratio fall within the bracket.
stability_protocol_SP-101-02.pdf.post_approval_commitment: The first three commercial batches will be placed on long-term stability post-approval and one batch per year thereafter.

stability_protocol_SP-204-01.pdf.acceptance_criteria: Assay 90.0-110.0%; impurity S-2 NMT 0.5%; water content NMT 5.0%
stability_protocol_SP-204-01.pdf.deviations: No deviations have been recorded to date.
stability_protocol_SP-204-01.pdf.bracketing_justification: Bracketing is not applied; all strengths and pack sizes are tested.
stability_protocol_SP-204-01.pdf.post_approval_commitment: One production batch per year will be added to the annual stability program.

stability_protocol_SP-509-03.pdf.acceptance_criteria: Assay 95.0-105.0%; oxidative degradant D-3 NMT 0.2%; pH 4.5-5.5; preservative content 80-110% of label
stability_protocol_SP-509-03.pdf.deviations: Deviation DEV-2026-022: refrigerator excursion to 11C for 4 hours on 2026-02-14; samples retained and results evaluated as within specification.
stability_protocol_SP-509-03.pdf.bracketing_justification: Bracketing is applied to the 60 mL and 240 mL bottle fills based on identical container closure materials; the 120 mL fill is bracketed.
stability_protocol_SP-509-03.pdf.post_approval_commitment: The in-use stability study requested under FDA-2025-1120 will be conducted on the first commercial batch.

stability_protocol_SP-611-01.pdf.acceptance_criteria: Assay 95.0-105.0%; disintegration NMT 30 seconds; hardness 20-40 N; total degradants NMT 1.5%
stability_protocol_SP-611-01.pdf.deviations: No deviations have been recorded to date.
stability_protocol_SP-611-01.pdf.bracketing_justification: Matrixing, rather than bracketing, is applied across blister strengths per ICH Q1D.
stability_protocol_SP-611-01.pdf.post_approval_commitment: None stated beyond the routine annual batch placement.
